title: dynamic batching: sequence-length bucketing + padding-minimization heuristics (v6)
description: Motivation: reduce wasted compute caused by padding in continuous batching when there is high variance in request sequence lengths. This PR implements a sequence-length bucketing optimizer and padding-minimization heuristics that integrate with the continuous-batcher and the smart scheduler. The change introduces a lightweight adaptive bucketing policy that maintains per-model sequence-length histograms, uses a sliding-window estimator for hot buckets, and emits bucket assignments for incoming requests to minimize cross-batch padding. It also adds an optional padding-aware kernel selector that prefers kernels optimized for similar-seqlen groups. The PR includes conservative fallbacks to preserve latency SLOs: when bucketization would increase p99 or wait time above configured thresholds we fall back to the previous greedy batching policy. Work items completed: adaptive histogram, bucketing policy, scheduler integration, KV-cache alignment to avoid cache fragmentation across buckets, padding-aware kernel hinting, end-to-end perf tests, and docs. Performance summary: +12% throughput on mixed-seqlen chat workload (avg seq 32/128 mix), ~8% token-cost reduction in steady-state, p99 latency impact within +2ms in canary regions, 95th percentile wait-time reduced by 18% for mixed workloads. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime.dynamic_batching.v6 and disabled by default; gradual canary on internal perf cluster then opt-in customers before wider rollout. Related linear tickets: ENG-8213, ENG-8340. Backward compatibility: no breaking API changes; config flags documented. Checklist: - [x] design doc and benchmarks - [x] unit/integration tests - [x] canary performance runs - [x] docs/cli flags - [x] security review (no secrets)

release_notes: Introduce adaptive sequence-length bucketing and padding-minimization heuristics for dynamic batching. Opt-in feature behind runtime.dynamic_batching.v6 with conservative fallbacks. Improves throughput and reduces token cost for mixed sequence-length workloads.
